name: Gweike G6 Split 100W
tagline: 100W Split cabinet fiber marker with room for rotary and fixtures
tldr: Gweike G6 Split 100W is the 100W SKU on the Gweike gweike g6 split line. Gweike G6 Split is a larger fiber marking platform with separate laser source cabinet: common format for small production. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Maximum fiber marking speed and depth in the line

priceRange.note: 100W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

pros: Fastest G6 Split in our benchmark: about 2–5 min for a filled 10 × 10 cm logo on stainless
Enough power to keep deep work practical on the 300 × 300 mm lens
$300–400 less than the G6 Split MOPA 100W
cons: $6,299 to $6,699: over $1,000 more than the 70W for a modest gain on surface marking
No MOPA pulse control: no colour marking despite the top power
Deep, high-power jobs produce a lot of fumes and spatter: extraction is not optional

faq.question: What is the G6 Split 100W best used for?
faq.answer: Production deep engraving and cut-outs on metal: embossed logos, deep serial numbers on tools, coins and thin-sheet parts. In our benchmark a filled 10 × 10 cm logo on stainless takes about 2–5 minutes, the quickest of the G6 Split range. For light surface marking the extra power changes little.

faq.question: How much does the G6 Split 100W cost, and with which options?
faq.answer: On Gweike's US store in October 2026: $6,299 with manual lift, $6,399 with electric lift and $6,699 with electric lift and autofocus. The colour-capable G6 Split MOPA 100W costs $6,599–7,099 in the same three configurations.

faq.question: Standard 100W or G6 Split MOPA 100W?
faq.answer: The standard 100W uses a Raycus Q-switched source with fixed pulses: good value for depth and black marking. The MOPA version, $300–400 more, adds adjustable pulse width for colour on stainless and cleaner marks on plastics and anodized aluminum. If colour work is not part of what you sell, the standard model is the cheaper route to 100W.

standoutFeatures.title: Highest throughput in the G6 Split range
standoutFeatures.body: About 2–5 minutes for a filled 10 × 10 cm logo on stainless in our benchmark, and the most headroom for multi-pass cut-outs and embossing on tools and plates.

standoutFeatures.title: Power for large-field lenses
standoutFeatures.body: A 300 × 300 mm lens spreads energy over a larger spot. With 100W, deep engraving stays workable on large plates where the lower tiers slow down sharply.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 100W SKU on Gweike G6 Split. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Push speed only after depth tests on your metal alloy. Cooling and lens cleanliness matter more at this power level.
primaryUse: High-power fiber for metal-focused shops needing line-top throughput

editorialDepth.advantages: Gweike G6 Split 100W fits shops that mark stainless, aluminum, and tools daily without a CO₂ bay. A solid bench option for jewelry, tags, and small batches.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if wood, leather, or cast acrylic pay your bills. Deep metal cutting and large industrial panels often need more fiber headroom or a different machine class.
